dataset.note: the whole-snapshot digest binds the producer's manifest (schema, suite sha, dataset set); per-benchmark row snapshots are the content check

known_differences: prompt_contract_sha256 and request_sha256 bind generation settings that include model_id and seed, so raw agreement across models (or seeds) is 0 by construction; compare the neutral digests instead.
T's served view lacks <|endoftext|> (151643) as an extra stop id; B and V list it (DESIGN.md section 3).

V's native chat template replaces the system message with a ~490-token reasoning prompt and pre-fills '<think>\n'; its prompt tokens are longer although prompt_sha256 (the pre-template message payload) matches.

The archive's dataset_sha256 (producer dataset manifest) differs from the prepared clone's whole-manifest digest; row identity is checked per row against the clone manifest instead (see 'dataset'). The neutral prompt-contract digest binds dataset_sha256, so it differs between archived and local rows by construction.

The existing local reruns were served from the protocol clone's prepared commit snapshots (each local run report's served_model.served_view records the file set and its content revision). For T this is the full 18-file snapshot, while the archived T used the content-bound 10-file runtime view recorded in manifests/model_roles.json (sha256set:8396b0be...). Prompt tokens agree on every row, but the T drift comparison conflates hardware with this view difference.

Archived parts record the producer's code identity (producer_code_revision / producer_code_sha256); local runs record the spool's trace_git_commit and final25_code_hash. Both are listed under 'scorer_code', not assumed equal.

Every local rerun shares its sampling seed with the archived slice it is compared with, so its row-score agreement and identical-text rate mix seed coupling with environment drift; the archived seed pairs use different seeds and bound resampling noise only.

scorers.note: scorer ids are forced to '<benchmark>-primary-v1' by ingestion; scorer code identity is under 'scorer_code'
